title: Episodic chatflow cost prescriptions
content:
Purpose
This memo captures a set of practical presets and rationale for optimizing cost and latency for "episodic" conversational workloads (many short turns per session, occasional long context replay). The goal is a lightweight set of recommended defaults we can ship in Optimize as workload presets and a companion cost-model spreadsheet to validate savings across representative customers.

Context and assumptions
- Workload: chat apps with median request length 18 tokens, 90th percentile 160 tokens, 1.8 requests per active session minute, typical session lifespan 10 minutes.
- Models considered: open-family vicuna/llama-like 13B and 70B variants, and a 7B low-precision candidate.
- Hardware: A100-80GB and H100 pools (hosted + dedicated).
- SLOs: primary target p95 latency <= 350ms for interactive turns; tail latency and throughput matter for scale.
- Baseline: no qcache, default batching (batch_size=16), float16 serving for 13B/70B, float32 for critical ops.

Synthesis of profiling observations (short)
- Short-turn dominance means steady-state token rate is low per request but turn frequency is moderate.
- KV cache hit rates are only meaningful if we cache session prefixes (system prompt + previous 2 turns) rather than entire sessions because sessions are often pruned and user text varies.
- Quantization yields biggest cost wins on 70B with small quality regression on narrow-turn prompts. 13B shows modest wins; 7B is dominated by throughput improvement but small accuracy delta.

Recommended presets (episodic-chatflow-default)
1) Batching & queueing
   - target_dynamic_batching: enabled
   - preferred_batch_size_range: 4-12 (start at 6 for latency-sensitive tiers)
   - max_queue_delay_ms: 40 (aggressive hedging to keep p95 low)
   - small-request-pass-through: enable for requests where token count <= 24 and user-specified latency tier = interactive
   Rationale: Lower batch sizes reduce queuing latency while still allowing small aggregation. For A100 hardware, a batch of 6 shows near-linear per-token efficiency gains for 13B.

2) Prefix/KV caching
   - prefix_checkpointing: store system + last 2 user/assistant turns per session
   - kv_cache_ttl_minutes: 15 (evict after 15 min inactivity)
   - cachewarm_policy: warm on session resume only if session_length > 3 turns
   - cache_size_limit_per_gpu_mb: 1200 (protect memory headroom)
   Rationale: Caching only stable prefixes reduces cache churn and increases hit rate for repeated assistant-style prompts or instruction templates. TTL tuned for typical episodic session lifespan.

3) Quantization profiles
   - 70B: q4_0 for production burstable + q8_0 for dedicated steady-state; enable automatic fallback to fp16 if eval regression > 1.5% on critical eval set
   - 13B: q4_0 preferred for cost-sensitive customers; q5_0 for high-quality tier
   - 7B: q3_k for max throughput; fallback rarely needed
   - q-merge-window-tokens: 256 (don't apply aggressive per-layer requant until prefix > 256 tokens)
   Rationale: 70B quant brings largest absolute cost savings. Use two-tier qprofile to keep a high-quality fallback available. Merge window avoids small-context quant artifacts.

4) Routing and fallback policy
   - route_by_latency_sla: interactive requests -> smaller batches + qprofile priority = high-quality; throughput/background -> larger batches + aggressive quant
   - fallback_chain: primary model (quantized 70B) -> fast 13B quantized -> 7B low-precision when capacity constrained
   Rationale: Keep interactive quality while reducing cost by routing degraded requests to cheaper variants automatically during sustained overloads.

5) Client-visible controls (API knobs we recommend exposing)
   - priority: interactive | standard | background
   - quality_hint: balanced | cost_saving | max_quality
   - session_cache_preference: aggressive | default | off
   Short examples: priority=interactive + quality_hint=balanced => small batch, prefix caching, q4 profiling on 13B.

Simulated cost model summary (high level)
- Spreadsheet assumptions: token pricing modeled per GPU-hour amortized by throughput; added per-request overhead for small-turns; network egress excluded. The attached cost_model sheet (linked artifact) uses per-token microcosts derived from profiler runs.
- Representative outcome: Compared to baseline (batch_size=16, no cache, fp16 13B/70B):
   * episodic-chatflow-default reduces per-turn cost by ~32% for 70B-heavy traffic and ~18% for 13B-dominant traffic.
   * p95 latency impact is neutral or improved by the smaller starting batch size + max_queue_delay_ms.

Known risks and quality checks
- Regression risk: quantization can cause subtle divergence on long context reasoning. Add a nightly eval job that runs an episodic-chat test-suite and flags >1% drop in answer fidelity.
- Cache correctness: prefix caching must respect user privacy and prompt-sanitization rules—work with security to enforce redaction and opt-out paths.
- Edge cases: sessions with heavy multimodal attachments or very long transcripts should bypass prefix caching and use larger-batch, high-memory nodes.

Operational checklist for rollout (MVP -> GA)
- MVP (canary): ship preset to 10% of traffic for two customers with known episodic patterns. Monitor: p95 latency, cache hit rate, quant-fallback events, per-token unit cost.
- Mid rollout: expand to 50% after two-week stability, collect user feedback on quality hints.
- GA: document preset in Console with a one-click apply and include recommended spreadsheet run for cost projection.

Open questions / TODOs
- Run targeted A/B for q4_0 vs q8_0 on our 70B regression harness to quantify quality delta on episodic prompt types. (JIRA-MLOPS-4127)
- Evaluate whether a session-adaptive batcher (shrink batch size near session start) yields extra tail latency improvement.
- Confirm telemetry fields to add to Console dashboard (cache_hit_rate_by_session, q_fallback_count, per_priority_costs).

Next steps and owners
- Maya: assemble the episodic-chat cost spreadsheet (baseline & scenario tabs) and link to this doc. Target: 2025-03-07.
- Arjun: run quant A/B for 70B on episodic harness and report quality delta. Target: 2025-03-14.
- Lina: prototype prefix checkpointing TTL and eviction heuristics in runtime sandbox. Target: 2025-03-10.

Appendix (short config snippets)
- example route config: { priority: \"interactive\", batch: { min:4, max:12, max_queue_ms:40 }, cache: { ttl_min:15, include_turns:2 }, qprofile: \"q4_0\" }
- recommended eval checklist: nightly episodic-harness, 1k sessions, measure: p95 latency, top-1 semantic overlap, hallucination rate, cost per active session.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: sets defaults we can change without platform release. Please flag any model-specific quality concerns or obvious security constraints.
